tools.name: api_resources_list
tools.description: Look up the Kubernetes API resource type(s) matching a specific kind you already have in mind (apiVersion, plural resource name, whether namespaced), using the server's preferred version for each match -- the same data 'kubectl api-resources' shows for that kind. Use this to discover the correct apiVersion for a kind before calling resources_get, resources_list, resources_create_or_update, resources_delete, or resources_scale, especially for CRDs whose apiVersion isn't already known.

kind.description: Required case-insensitive exact filter on kind (e.g. 'Deployment', 'Route'). Matches the same Kind across every API group and version, so the result can still contain multiple API resource entries.

tools.name: events_list
tools.description: List Kubernetes events (warnings, errors, state changes) for debugging and troubleshooting in the current cluster from all namespaces. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter events by field values (e.g. 'type=Warning', 'involvedObject.name=my-pod'). Supported fields: involvedObject.kind, involvedObject.name, involvedObject.namespace, involvedObject.uid, involvedObject.apiVersion, involvedObject.resourceVersion, involvedObject.fieldPath, reason, reportingComponent, source, type. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the events from. If not provided, will list events from all namespaces

tools.name: helm_install
tools.description: Install (deploy) a Helm chart to create a release in the current or provided namespace

chart.description: Chart reference to install (for example: stable/grafana, oci://ghcr.io/nginxinc/charts/nginx-ingress)

name.description: Name of the Helm release (Optional, random name if not provided)

namespace.description: Namespace to install the Helm chart in (Optional, current namespace if not provided)

values.description: Values to pass to the Helm chart (Optional)

tools.name: helm_list
tools.description: List all the Helm releases in the current or provided namespace (or in all namespaces if specified). Use limit and offset to page the releases returned to you. Helm loads release secrets before applying that page, so a secret list that exceeds max_backend_response_bytes can still fail.

all_namespaces.description: If true, lists all Helm releases in all namespaces ignoring the namespace argument (Optional)

limit.description: Maximum number of releases to return. Omit or set to 0 to return every release Helm loaded. A full page tells you the next offset.

namespace.description: Namespace to list Helm releases from (Optional, all namespaces if not provided)

offset.description: Number of releases to skip. Send the next offset from a full page, with the same limit.

tools.name: helm_uninstall
tools.description: Uninstall a Helm release in the current or provided namespace

name.description: Name of the Helm release to uninstall

namespace.description: Namespace to uninstall the Helm release from (Optional, current namespace if not provided)

tools.name: namespaces_list
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes namespaces in the current cluster. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter namespaces by field values (e.g. 'metadata.name=default', 'status.phase=Active'). Supported fields: metadata.name, status.phase. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

tools.name: nodes_log
tools.description: Get logs from a Kubernetes node (kubelet, kube-proxy, or other system logs). This accesses node logs through the Kubernetes API proxy to the kubelet

name.description: Name of the node to get logs from

query.description: query specifies services(s) or files from which to return logs (required). Example: "kubelet" to fetch kubelet logs, "/<log-file-name>" to fetch a specific log file from the node (e.g., "/var/log/kubelet.log" or "/var/log/kube-proxy.log")

tailLines.description: Number of lines to retrieve from the end of the logs (Optional, 0 means all logs)

tools.name: nodes_stats_summary
tools.description: Get detailed resource usage statistics from a Kubernetes node via the kubelet's Summary API. Provides comprehensive metrics including CPU, memory, filesystem, and network usage at the node, pod, and container levels. On systems with cgroup v2 and kernel 4.20+, also includes PSI (Pressure Stall Information) metrics that show resource pressure for CPU, memory, and I/O. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/understand-psi-metrics/ for details on PSI metrics

name.description: Name of the node to get stats from

tools.name: nodes_top
tools.description: List the resource consumption (CPU and memory) as recorded by the Kubernetes Metrics Server for the specified Kubernetes Nodes or all nodes in the cluster. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

label_selector.description: Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'node-role.kubernetes.io/worker=') to filter nodes by label (Optional, only applicable when name is not provided)

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

name.description: Name of the Node to get the resource consumption from (Optional, all Nodes if not provided)

tools.name: pods_delete
tools.description: Delete a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided name

name.description: Name of the Pod to delete

namespace.description: Namespace to delete the Pod from

tools.name: pods_exec
tools.description: Execute a command in a Kubernetes Pod (shell access, run commands in container) in the current or provided namespace with the provided name and command

command.description: Command to execute in the Pod container. The first item is the command to be run, and the rest are the arguments to that command. Example: ["ls", "-l", "/tmp"]

container.description: Name of the Pod container where the command will be executed (Optional)

name.description: Name of the Pod where the command will be executed

namespace.description: Namespace of the Pod where the command will be executed

tools.description: Get a Kubernetes Pod in the current or provided namespace with the provided name

namespace.description: Namespace to get the Pod from

tools.name: pods_list
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes pods in the current cluster from all namespaces. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter pods by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'spec.nodeName=node1'). limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

tools.name: pods_list_in_namespace
tools.description: List all the Kubernetes pods in the specified namespace in the current cluster. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter pods by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'spec.nodeName=node1'). tools.name: resources_create_or_update
tools.description:
Create or update a Kubernetes resource via Server-Side Apply. The manifest is the complete desired state: any field this tool previously set and the new manifest omits is removed. To edit an existing resource, fetch it with resources_get, modify it, then re-apply the full resource.
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

resource.description: Complete YAML or JSON representation of the Kubernetes resource (full desired state, not a partial patch). Include apiVersion, kind, metadata, and the full spec.

tools.name: resources_delete
tools.description:
Delete a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, optionally the namespace, and its name
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

gracePeriodSeconds.description: Optional duration in seconds before the object should be deleted. Value must be non-negative integer. The value zero indicates delete immediately. If this value is nil, the default grace period for the specified type will be used

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to delete the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will delete resource from configured namespace

tools.name: resources_get
tools.description:
Get a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, optionally the namespace, and its name
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resource from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will get resource from configured namespace

tools.name: resources_list
tools.description:
List Kubernetes resources and objects in the current cluster by providing their apiVersion and kind and optionally the namespace and label selector. Use limit and continue to retrieve a large list one page at a time.
(common apiVersion and kind include: v1 Pod, v1 Service, v1 Node, apps/v1 Deployment, networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress, route.openshift.io/v1 Route)

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resources (examples of valid apiVersion are: v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1)

continue.description: Opaque token from the continue field of the previous page. Send it unchanged with the same limit, namespace, and selectors to retrieve the next page. Omit on the first call.

fieldSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes field selector to filter resources by field values (e.g. 'status.phase=Running', 'metadata.name=myresource'). Supported fields vary by resource type. For Pods: metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.restartPolicy, spec.schedulerName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.phase (Pending/Running/Succeeded/Failed/Unknown), status.podIP, status.nominatedNodeName. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/field-selectors/

kind.description: kind of the resources (examples of valid kind are: Pod, Service, Deployment, Ingress)

labelSelector.description: Optional Kubernetes label selector (e.g. 'app=myapp,env=prod' or 'app in (myapp,yourapp)'), use this option when you want to filter the resources by label

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return. Omit or set to 0 to list everything, which fails if the response exceeds max_backend_response_bytes. Retry with a smaller limit when that happens. The API may return fewer items than requested.

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to retrieve the namespaced resources from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will list resources from all namespaces

tools.name: resources_scale
tools.description: Get or update the scale of a Kubernetes resource in the current cluster by providing its apiVersion, kind, name, and optionally the namespace. If the scale is set in the tool call, the scale will be updated to that value. Always returns the current scale of the resource

apiVersion.description: apiVersion of the resource (examples of valid apiVersion are apps/v1)

kind.description: kind of the resource (examples of valid kind are: StatefulSet, Deployment)

namespace.description: Optional Namespace to get/update the namespaced resource scale from (ignored in case of cluster scoped resources). If not provided, will get/update resource scale from configured namespace

scale.description: Optional scale to update the resources scale to. If not provided, will return the current scale of the resource, and not update it

  name: webapp
  namespace: orders

  progressDeadlineSeconds: 600
  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 10
  selector:

    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp

      containers:
      - name: webapp
        image: quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:latest

        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
          protocol: TCP
        livenessProbe:
          failureThreshold: 3

            path: /get_status
            port: 8080
            scheme: HTTP
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
          successThreshold: 1
          timeoutSeconds: 1

          failureThreshold: 3
          httpGet:

            port: 8080
            scheme: HTTP
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
          successThreshold: 1
          timeoutSeconds: 1
        resources: {}
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
        terminationMessagePolicy: File
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
      restartPolicy: Always
      schedulerName: default-scheduler
      securityContext: {}
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
  namespace: orders
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        image: quay.io/nginx/nginx-unprivileged:latest
        imagePullPolicy: Always
        ports:
        - name: http
          containerPort: 8080
          protocol: TCP
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 8080
            scheme: HTTP
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 8080
            scheme: HTTP
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5

Steps.message:
namespace/web created
deployment.apps/nginx created
service/nginx created

The Service’s selector was the problem: it selected `app=web`, but the nginx pod is labeled `app=nginx`. That left the Service without a matching backend. I changed the selector to `app=nginx`.

The Service now has an endpoint at `10.244.0.27:8080`. Its port mapping (`80` → `8080`) is consistent with the unprivileged nginx image. It’s a `ClusterIP` Service, so it’s reachable from inside the cluster at `nginx.web.svc.cluster.local:80` (or `10.99.30.128:80`), but isn’t exposed externally.

The Service’s selector was the problem: it selected `app=web`, but the nginx pod is labeled `app=nginx`. That left the Service without a matching backend. I changed the selector to `app=nginx`.

The Service now has an endpoint at `10.244.0.27:8080`. Its port mapping (`80` → `8080`) is consistent with the unprivileged nginx image. It’s a `ClusterIP` Service, so it’s reachable from inside the cluster at `nginx.web.svc.cluster.local:80` (or `10.99.30.128:80`), but isn’t exposed externally.

The pods were stuck in `Pending` because the Deployment required `nodeSelector: environment: production-gpu`, but the cluster’s only node (`mcp-eval-cluster`) doesn’t have that label. With no pods scheduled, the Service had no healthy backends, causing the connection refusals.

I removed the restrictive node selector. The Deployment now has **2/2 pods Running and Ready**, and `web-app-service` has both pod IPs on port 80 as endpoints. The service should now accept connections.

outputSteps.content:
The pods were stuck in `Pending` because the Deployment required `nodeSelector: environment: production-gpu`, but the cluster’s only node (`mcp-eval-cluster`) doesn’t have that label. With no pods scheduled, the Service had no healthy backends, causing the connection refusals.

I removed the restrictive node selector. The Deployment now has **2/2 pods Running and Ready**, and `web-app-service` has both pod IPs on port 80 as endpoints. The service should now accept connections.

results.taskOutput:
Created the six requested namespaces, developer service accounts, namespace RoleBindings, ResourceQuotas, and NetworkPolicies.

- **Developer access:** Alice, Bob, and Charlie each have the built-in `admin` role in their own namespace. Their matching service accounts are bound there too.
- **Shared access:** The developers and all three service accounts have the built-in `view` role in `dev-shared`.
- **Staging and prod:** No developer access bindings were added. Each namespace has a quota and a policy restricting pod traffic to that same namespace and `kube-system`.
- **Quotas:** Developer namespaces are capped at 2 CPUs, 4 GiB memory, 10 pods, and 5 services; `dev-shared` at 4 CPUs, 8 GiB, 20 pods, and 10 services; staging/prod at 8 CPUs, 16 GiB, 50 pods, and 20 services. CPU and memory limits and requests are both capped.
- **Network isolation:** Policies in all six namespaces restrict traffic to the permitted namespace peers and `kube-system`; this also provides default-deny ingress and egress for selected pods in those namespaces.

**Important checks before relying on this in production:** NetworkPolicies are enforced only if the cluster’s CNI supports them. The egress exception currently permits traffic to any pod in `kube-system` (to allow DNS and system services); narrow that to specific system-service pods and ports if you can confirm their labels and requirements. Also review existing cluster-wide RBAC bindings: they can grant users access to staging or prod despite the absence of namespace RoleBindings here.

outputSteps.content:
Created the six requested namespaces, developer service accounts, namespace RoleBindings, ResourceQuotas, and NetworkPolicies.

- **Developer access:** Alice, Bob, and Charlie each have the built-in `admin` role in their own namespace. Their matching service accounts are bound there too.
- **Shared access:** The developers and all three service accounts have the built-in `view` role in `dev-shared`.
- **Staging and prod:** No developer access bindings were added. Each namespace has a quota and a policy restricting pod traffic to that same namespace and `kube-system`.
- **Quotas:** Developer namespaces are capped at 2 CPUs, 4 GiB memory, 10 pods, and 5 services; `dev-shared` at 4 CPUs, 8 GiB, 20 pods, and 10 services; staging/prod at 8 CPUs, 16 GiB, 50 pods, and 20 services. CPU and memory limits and requests are both capped.
- **Network isolation:** Policies in all six namespaces restrict traffic to the permitted namespace peers and `kube-system`; this also provides default-deny ingress and egress for selected pods in those namespaces.

**Important checks before relying on this in production:** NetworkPolicies are enforced only if the cluster’s CNI supports them. The egress exception currently permits traffic to any pod in `kube-system` (to allow DNS and system services); narrow that to specific system-service pods and ports if you can confirm their labels and requirements. Also review existing cluster-wide RBAC bindings: they can grant users access to staging or prod despite the absence of namespace RoleBindings here.

      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
